rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative ‘this’ points back to the preceding statement that the keepers of Hell are nineteen.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بهذا إلى قوله : { عليها تسعة عشر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثلا is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of هذا; المثل means a description, asking why this number rather than another such as twenty.
rows.anchor: و { مثلا } منصوب على الحال من هذا ، والمثل : الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, المثل describes the extraordinary situation of Hell’s keepers being nineteen, as in the description of Paradise.
rows.anchor: والمثل : وصف الحالة العجيبة ، أي ما وصفه من عدد خزنة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك refers to the preceding whole account, from the scripture recipients’ certainty through the question about the example, construed as what was mentioned.
rows.anchor: اسم الإشارة عائد إلى ما تضمنه الكلام المتقدم من قوله

words: يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with diseased hearts and disbelievers are led astray, including scripture recipients who became certain but did not believe; believers are guided and their faith grows.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الضلال الحاصل للذين في قلوبهم مرض وللكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison brings the abstract divine creation of human circumstances close through a familiar concrete event, teaching Muslims to seek what benefits their souls.
rows.anchor: والغرض من هذا التشبيه تقريب المعنى المعقول وهو تصرف الله تعالى

words: يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness is causation: God makes both guidance and misguidance causes for a wisdom grounded in His knowledge; people’s receptivity ranges from guidance to doubt, denial, and misunderstanding.
rows.anchor: ووجه الشبه هو السببية في اهتداء من يهتدي وضلال من يضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact comparison encompasses many outward patterns, as dispositions lead from soundness to soundness, uncertainty to uncertainty, or resentment and stubbornness to further error.
rows.anchor: فانطوى التشبيه من قوله : { كذلك } على أحوال وصور كثيرة

words: يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s attribution of misguidance reflects His creation of original dispositions, desires, worldly interconnections, prophetic invitations, and the resistance of leaders of error; all are created by God.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الإضلال إلى الله تعالى باعتبار أنه موجد الأسباب الأصلية في الجبلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Souls that seek good and salvation must expose themselves to one of the two paths after reflection; each bears what it has earned.
rows.anchor: فما على الأنفس المريدة الخير والنجاة إلا التعرض لأحد المهيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s will in this matter is connected to His knowledge of the course the guided and misguided will follow.
rows.anchor: ومشيئة الله ذلك تعلق علمه بسلوك المهتدين والضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك is an adverbial phrase standing for an omitted cognate accusative: misguidance and guidance of this kind; it is not the construction in 2:143.
rows.anchor: ومحل { كذلك } نصب بالنيابة عن المفعول المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the cognate-object description stresses the comparison; it also creates an initial grouping followed by division into misguidance and guidance.
rows.anchor: وقدم وصف المفعول المطلق للاهتمام بهذا التشبيه

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This comprehensive coda refutes the speculations of disbelievers and the spiritually ill about reports of the unseen and afterlife, including Abu Jahl’s question about Hell’s keepers.
rows.anchor: كلمة جامعة لإبطال التخرصات التي يتخرصها الضالون ومرضى القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنود is the plural of جند, a troop or army; metaphorically it means creatures God appoints to carry out His command, like an army executing orders.
rows.anchor: والجنود : جمع جند وهو اسم لجماعة الجيش واستعير هنا للمخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding ‘your Lord’ to the Prophet’s pronoun honors him and hints that some of these forces will support the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وإضافة رب إلى ضمير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إضافة تشريف

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negation concerns detailed knowledge of the forces’ numbers, qualities, and properties; people know the keepers’ number because God disclosed it.
rows.anchor: ونفي العلم هنا نفي للعلم التفصيلي بأعدادها وصفاتها وخصائصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost reading continues the statement that their number is a test: the useful lesson is to remember punishment, since describing a thing helps bring it to mind; scoffers instead debate the number.
rows.anchor: أعلاها أن يكون هذا تتمة لقوله : { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading, هي refers to the number of the keepers.
rows.anchor: وضمير { هي } على هذا الوجه إلى { عدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to the preceding discourse, understood as the story, description, or Quranic verses; the sense remains similar.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يرجع الضمير إلى الكلام السابق وتأنيث ضميره لتأويله بالقصة أو الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that هي refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder through its threat and horrors; an omitted noun such as its mention or description is understood.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع إلى سقر } ( المدثر : 26 ) وإنما تكون { ذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the forces of the Lord, with the omitted sense being their mention or the number of some of them.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع ضمير { هي } إلى { جنود ربك }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows هي to refer to earthly fire, which reminds people of the fire of the afterlife, as in the verse calling fire a reminder.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزجاج أن يكون الضمير راجعا إلى نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the earthly-fire reading, the expression uses semantic redirection (istikhdām).
rows.anchor: وفيه محسن الاستخدام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the number reminds people that God needs no helpers, so they should not wonder how nineteen can face Hell’s many inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى : وما عدتهم إلا ذكرى للناس ليعلموا غنى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context accommodates these readings through the eloquence of Quranic arrangement; after 74:29 the pronoun would unambiguously refer to Saqar, showing the effect of sentence placement.
rows.anchor: ولو وقعت إثر قوله : { لواحة للبشر } ( المدثر : 29 ) لتمحض ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One scholarly view holds that resurrection regathers the same bodies’ scattered particles, in which case نجمع is literal.
rows.anchor: وهو أحد قولين لعلمائنا ، ففعل { نجمع } محمول على حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view holds that God creates bodies matching the vanished bodies, either afresh or from the coccyx bone as some reports state; نجمع is then metaphorical for that recreation.
rows.anchor: ففعل { نجمع } مستعار للخلق الذي هو على صورة الجسم الذي بلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor echoes the opponents’ wording and avoids detailing how resurrection occurs; Quranic accounts stay general, and Muslim scholars consequently differed about bodily restoration.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة استعارته مشاكلة أقوال المشركين التي أريد إبطالها

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: The Imam of the Two Sanctuaries suspended judgment on how bodies are restored; Quranic verses accommodate both scholarly accounts.
rows.anchor: واختار إمام الحرمين التوقف ، وآيات القرآن ورد فيها ما يصلح للأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلى cancels the negation implied by ‘We will not gather his bones’: indeed, they will be gathered under either account of resurrection.
rows.anchor: { بلى } حرف إبطال للنفي الذي دل عليه { لن نجمع عظامه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قادرين can be circumstantial from the implied subject of a verb after بلى, supplied by the preceding words: God gathers the bones while able to restore fingertips.
rows.anchor: { قادرين } حال من الضمير في الفعل المحذوف بعد { بلى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, بلى rejects both the rhetorical question’s implied denial and the denial within its object; قادرين is then the second object of an implied ‘reckon Us’, with the shift to fingertip restoration giving fuller meaning while keeping resurrection’s manner general.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { بلى } إبطالا للنفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is not read in the nominative قادرون on an implied نحن قادرون construction.
rows.anchor: وعدل في متعلق { قادرين } عن أن يقال : قادرين على جمع عظامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswiyah means straightening and making creation precise; restoring the fingertips finely is a metonym for creating them, since nothing is made well-proportioned without being recreated.
rows.anchor: والتسوية : تقويم الشيء وإتقان الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise phrase became proverbial because it packs many meanings into few words.
rows.anchor: وقد جرت هذه الجملة مجرى المثل لإيجازها ووفرة معانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولو ألقى معاذيره is a circumstantial clause describing الإنسان, a state that especially confirms the main assertion when it occurs.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولو ألقى معاذيره } في موضع الحال من المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لو is concessive: a person sees his own state even while presenting excuses, as in the cited usage in 3:91.
rows.anchor: { لو } هذه وصلية كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى : { فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلقاء (casting) is metaphorical for openly reporting; the author compares the usage with a Quranic phrase in al-Nahl.
rows.anchor: والإلقاء : مراد به الإخبار الصريح على وجه الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معاذير is a collective plural meaning excuses, not the regular plural معاذر; المناكير is a similar collective noun.
rows.anchor: والمعاذير : اسم جمع معذرة ، وليس جمعا لأن معذرة حقه أن يجمع على معاذر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says معاذير is plural of معذار, a Yemeni word for a veil; casting is literal lowering, while excuses metaphorically veil the matter being hidden.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك : أن معاذير هنا جمع معذار بكسر الميم وهو الستر بلغة اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned person knows the deeds deserving punishment and tries to excuse himself, while knowing no excuse can vindicate him even if he states every one.
rows.anchor: أن الكافر يعلم يومئذ أعماله التي استحق العقاب عليها ويحاول أن يعتذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural denotes all excuses, including pleas to return and do good, denial that a warner came, and blaming those who led them astray.
rows.anchor: ومعاذيره } : جمع معرف بالإضافة يدل على العموم . فمن هذه المعاذير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the Bukhari and Muslim report, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet moved his tongue as revelation came to memorize it, fearing he might lose it and experiencing strain; God told him to listen as it was recited, then recite it, with its collection and explanation guaranteed.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها ما رواه البخاري ومسلم عن ابن عباس أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses were revealed during the surah’s revelation for their own purpose, then attached to the surah rather than forming an independent surah.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل هذا الوحي في أثناء نزول السورة للغرض الذي نزل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in به refers to the Quran, as it does in many Quranic passages.
rows.anchor: فضمير { به } عائد على القرآن كما هو المعروف في آيات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading is Gabriel’s reading on God’s behalf; attributing it to the divine pronoun is a clear case of figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: أي إذا قرأه جبريل عنا ، فأسندت القراءة إلى ضمير الجلالة على طريقة المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the recitation means listening attentively to it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { فاتبع قرآنه } ، أي أنصت إلى قراءتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in قرأناه refers to the same Quran as the pronoun in لا تحرك به, treating Quran as the thing read.
rows.anchor: فضمير { قرأناه } راجع إلى ما رجع إليه ضمير الغائب في { لا تحرك به }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage’s insertion resembles 19:64 and the prayer command in 2:238, which appears amid the marriage rulings of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: فيكون وقوع هذه الآية في هذه السورة مثل وقوع { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك } في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: أهل الحديث وأيمة التفسير
rows.claim: Hadith scholars and leading exegetes agree that these verses were revealed during the course of Surat al-Qiyama.
rows.anchor: قالوا : نزلت هذه الآية في أثناء سورة القيامة : هذا ما لا خلاف فيه بين أهل الحديث وأيمة التفسير

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reads the address as directed to the human being in 75:13 reading his record: God gathers and recites the deeds, he follows by acknowledging them, and God explains the levels of punishment; reason allows this though reports do not support it.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفخر عن القفال أنه قال : إن قوله : لا تحرك به لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reason alone does not rule out al-Qaffal’s reading, Arabic style and the meanings of the words weigh against it.
rows.anchor: والذي يلوح لي في موقع هذه الآية هنا دون أن تقع فيما سبق نزوله من السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet initially feared forgetting verses as the surahs multiplied to roughly thirty in Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s chronology; he moved his tongue from care to preserve exact wording, and God compassionately forbade the effort after guaranteeing preservation.
rows.anchor: فلما كثرت السور فبلغت زهاء ثلاثين حسب ما عده سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both places, قرآن is the verbal noun meaning recitation, like غفران and فرقان; Hassan ibn Thabit’s elegy for Uthman witnesses the usage قرآنا.
rows.anchor: و ( قرآن ) في الموضعين مصدر بمعنى القراءة مثل الغفران والفرقان ، قال حسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both clauses, علينا expresses God’s undertaking and guarantee.
rows.anchor: ولفظ { علينا } في الموضعين للتكفل والتعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks a higher rank, placing the guarantee of explanation above the guarantee of collecting and reciting the revelation.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } في { ثم إن علينا بيانه } للتراخي في الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees gathering revelation, its recitation, and—above that—its explanation by the Prophet, preserved in his heart and clear to hearers without consulting a written copy.
rows.anchor: أن علينا جمع الوحي وأن تقرأه وفوق ذلك أن تبينه للناس بلسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here البيان means clarifying the Quran’s wording, not its meanings, since the meanings’ clarification accompanies the wording’s arrival.
rows.anchor: فالبيان هنا بيان ألفاظه وليس بيان معانيه

rows.speaker: بعض علمائنا
rows.claim: Some scholars use ثم here to argue that it is permissible to delay clarification after the matter being clarified.
rows.anchor: وقد احتج بهذه الآية بعض علمائنا الذين يرون جواز تأخير البيان عن المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That argument is weak: ثم indicates rank, coordinates the whole clause rather than بيان alone, and cannot imply that clarification is always delayed.
rows.anchor: لأن التراخي الذي أفادته { ثم } إنما هو تراخ في الرتبة لا في الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah returns to its main line after the interruption; كلا rebuts and invalidates the prior claims.
rows.anchor: رجوع إلى مهيع الكلام الذي بنيت عليه السورة كما يرجع المتكلم إلى وصل كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا may reject the claims from ‘Does man think We will not gather his bones?’ through ‘even if he offers excuses’; its repetition reconnects the discourse and means their claims are false.
rows.anchor: أن يكون إبطالا لما سبق من قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken literally, the two legs are wrapped together in the shroud after death; the definite article stands in place of a genitive complement, concluding the description of preparation for the grave.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى التفاف ساقي المحتضر بعد موته إذ تلف الأكفان على ساقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ساق is an Arabic figure for hardship, as in ‘war rose on a leg’; the phrase means one calamity has overtaken another.
rows.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس قول الراجز : صبرا عناق إنه لشرباق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas cites a rajaz poem whose line ‘the war rose upon a leg’ illustrates ساق as a metaphor for hardship.
rows.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس قول الراجز : صبرا عناق إنه لشرباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts from the plural audience in ‘you love the immediate life’ because that address is generic and unspecified, making variation apt.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { إلى ربك } التفات عن طريق خطاب الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The article in المساق is generic, encompassing everyone including the rejecting human; alternatively it replaces a genitive complement, the course of the man who asks when Resurrection will be.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { المساق } تعريف الجنس الذي يعم الناس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المساق is the mimetic verbal noun of ساق, leading someone before oneself toward a destination, opposed to القود; metaphorically it is bringing him to meet his Lord’s recompense.
rows.anchor: و { المساق } : مصدر ميمي ل ( ساق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended sentences after إذا magnify the disbeliever’s death throes and hint that he sees his fate at death.
rows.anchor: وسلك في الجمل التي بعد { إذا } مسلك الإطناب لتهويل حالة الاحتضار على الكافر

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: In a sound hadith, the Prophet says whoever loves meeting God is loved by God; ʿAisha or another wife objects that people dislike death, and he explains that believers receive glad tidings of favor and disbelievers of punishment at death, shaping their desire or aversion to meet God.
rows.anchor: وقد دل عليه حديث عبادة بن الصامت في ( الصحيح ) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage branches from the question ‘When is Resurrection?’; its subject is the human of 75:3, who failed to prepare because he did not understand resurrection.
rows.anchor: تفريع على قوله : { يسأل أيان يوم القيامة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of كذب is omitted to include everything the polytheists denied—the Messenger, Quran, and resurrection; تولى means refusing Islam’s laws.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { كذب } ليشمل كل ما كذب به المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the فاء connects to 75:30: the person has left life and is being taken to God without provisions for that meeting; the context implies his knowledge of loss and regret.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاء تفريعا وعطفا على قوله : { إلى ربك يومئذ المساق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied late realization and regret are stated in the passage where a person remembers after the earth is crushed and wishes he had sent ahead for his life.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد ذلك في قوله تعالى : { إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا وجاء ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صدق derives from taṣdīq, belief in the Messenger and Quran, fitting its contrast with ‘but he denied’.
rows.anchor: وفعل { صدق } مشتق من التصديق ، أي تصديق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take صدق to mean giving charity, but the regular form would be تصدق and that sense does not fit the contrast with denial.
rows.anchor: وبعض المفسرين فسر { صدق } بمعنى أعطى الصدقة ، وهو غير جار على قياس التصريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding ‘nor prayed’ alongside lack of belief makes his condition repugnant and unlike Muslims: he neither believed nor submitted.
rows.anchor: وعطف { ولا صلى } على نفس التصديق تشويها له

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i says لا can mean لم with past verbs when paired with another negation for two intended actions; Arabs say neither one nor the other, as in Zuhayr’s verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكسائي ( ( لا ) بمعنى ( لم ) ولكنه يقرن بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unpaired لا before a past verb is otherwise used for supplication or rarely; 90:11 is effectively repeated negation because ‘the obstacle’ entails freeing, feeding, and believing.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : { فلا اقتحم العقبة } ( البلد : 11 ) فإنه على تأويل تكرير النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولكن كذب is coordinated with فلا صدق. The ungeminated لكن is an inceptive conjunction, not the sister of إن that takes effect on case; it commonly follows a conjunction wāw.
rows.anchor: وحرف { لكن } المخفف لا يعمل إعرابا فهو حرف ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لكن can reinforce by stating the contrary, as in 33:5, or clarify an earlier general negation, as in 33:40.
rows.anchor: إما لمجرد توكيد المعنى بذكر نقيضه مثل قوله تعالى : { وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause both reinforces lack of belief through denial and clarifies deliberate turning away, since disbelief can arise in different ways; the author compares إبليس أبى واستكبر.
rows.anchor: أفادت معنيين : أحدهما توكيد قوله { فلا صدق } بقوله : { كذب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His denial concerns resurrection, the Quran, and Muhammad’s message.
rows.anchor: والتكذيب : تكذيبه بالبعث وبالقرآن وبرسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means rejecting the invitation to examine and reflect on the Quran.
rows.anchor: والتولي : الإعراض عن دعوته إلى النظر والتدبر في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of صدق and all the following verbs is the pronoun referring to the previously mentioned human.
rows.anchor: وفاعل { صدق } والأفعال المذكورة بعده ضمائر عائدة على الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتمطى means walking with المطياطى, that is, swaggering and strutting.
rows.anchor: و { يتمطى } : يمشي المطيطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form derives from يتمطط, to stretch out: the swaggerer lengthens his steps, walking in self-admiration.
rows.anchor: وأصل { يتمطى } : يتمطط ، أي يتمدد لأن المتبختر يمد خطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier neglected preparation for the afterlife, ignored the Messenger’s call, and went home swaggering without considering his fate; this concludes the description.
rows.anchor: أنه أهمل الاستعداد للآخرة ولم يعبأ بدعوة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports that most exegetes identify the passage beginning فلا صدق with Abu Jahl; يتمطى nearly names him because it was the Banu Makhzum gait and Abu Jahl often used it. Ibn Ashur signals an objection to this view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : قال جمهور المتأولين : هذه الآية كلها من قوله : { فلا صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولى لك is a fixed proverbial threat, though its person and number vary; like ويل لك, it wishes that harm be the nearest thing to the addressee.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { أولى لك } وعيد ، وهي كلمة توعد تجري مجرى المثل

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi explains فأولى as ‘what you hate has come near’; its omitted subject is understood by each listener as the feared thing, and the poet al-Khansa uses the phrase.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي : معناه : قاربك ما تكره ، قالت الخنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation connects the phrase with فأولى لهم in 47:20–21, taking طاعة وقول معروف as a new sentence rather than the subject of the comparative.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل : إن منه قوله تعالى : { فأولى لهم من قوله : فأولى لهم طاعة وقول معروف

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi treats أولى as a fixed word for woe/destruction, deriving it from أويل (more destructive) through metathesis for ease and a final weak-letter change.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو علي الفارسي إلى أن { أولى } علم لمعنى الويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person pronoun addresses the repeatedly mentioned human directly, shifting from third person to make the rebuke more forceful; the expected form would be أولى له.
rows.anchor: وعدل هنا عن طريق الغيبة إلى الخطاب على طريقة الالتفات
